findings.statement: a one-line fingerprint table routes at 85-100% of the perfect-routing ceiling
findings.detail: table16 174ns/read against oracle16 123 (table16 vs oracle16: less 0.707x (p=0.0216, rel_iqr 17.6%/9.8%)), 70.7% of the ceiling. Below the band even one global cache miss is too dear and per-segment blooms win by default; above it the measurement is suspect, not celebrated

findings.statement: the fingerprint table beats per-segment blooms outright
findings.detail: table16 174ns/read against bloom16 307 (table16 vs bloom16: greater 1.768x (p=0.0122, rel_iqr 17.6%/14.0%)); the table costs 13.11 B/key against the blooms' 1.25. If this is not a gated win, global routing is not worth its mutability concession at any price measured so far and the design keeps routing inside immutable per-segment state

notes: four arms interleaved in one process, same-run: k1, per-segment blooms (f40's structure to beat), the bucketized fingerprint table, and the oracle ceiling. The table is one 64-byte bucket load and a 16-way compare per query at load 0.5; a false fingerprint match falls back to the fan, so correctness never rests on it
